title: Practicing with Language Models Cultivates Human Empathic Communication
extended_summary:
The paper addresses whether large language models can help people improve empathic communication rather than replacing human empathy with AI-generated support. Prior work suggests LLMs can generate empathic responses that are often rated highly, but people feel less supported when they know a response comes from AI. The authors therefore ask whether LLMs can serve as practice partners and coaches to help humans better express empathy in text-based conversations.

The intervention was Lend an Ear, an online role-playing platform where participants practiced offering empathic support to LLM conversational partners describing workplace or personal troubles, such as job loss, being passed over for promotion, feeling undervalued at work, a parent’s cancer diagnosis, or bereavement. In a preregistered randomized experiment, 968 U.S. adults recruited through Prolific were assigned to one of four conditions: no feedback, short instructional videos, personalized feedback from an AI coach, or combined video plus AI coaching. Participants completed three text conversations, and their responses were evaluated on preregistered empathic communication dimensions such as encouraging elaboration, validating emotions, demonstrating understanding, avoiding unsolicited advice, avoiding self-oriented responses, and avoiding dismissive language.

The study found that personalized LLM feedback substantially improved expressed empathic communication compared with both control and video-only instruction. AI coaching increased prescriptive empathic behaviors and reduced several misattuned behaviors, especially unsolicited advice and dismissing emotions. The authors also found a disconnect between self-reported empathy or perceived empathic performance and actual expressed empathy, suggesting that people may feel empathy but lack the communicative skill to convey it effectively.

A second preregistered experiment with independent human raters showed that conversations scored more highly by LLM evaluators were also preferred by humans as more empathic, supporting the validity of the evaluation framework. Overall, the paper concludes that empathic communication can be treated as a learnable communicative skill and that brief, scalable LLM-based coaching can improve how people express empathy in controlled online practice settings.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model; in this paper GPT-4o was used to implement an LLM communication coach, LLM role-playing conversational partners, and LLM-based evaluation of empathic communication.
identified_tools.use_case: Used within the custom Lend an Ear platform so participants could practice empathic support in text conversations with LLM role-playing partners, receive personalized LLM-generated coaching feedback after conversations, and have their empathic communication scored on preregistered dimensions.

findings.finding_summary: In the preregistered randomized experiment with n=968 participants, personalized feedback from the AI coach produced a 0.98 SD increase, described as a 2.9-point gain, in overall empathic communication performance. Reliable improvement occurred for 21.6% of participants in the AI Coach condition versus 2.9% in control, with reliable decline of 0.4% versus 1.6%, respectively; combined training showed 26.3% reliable improvement.
findings.measure: Overall empathy score calculated as the sum of prescriptive behavior ratings minus proscriptive behavior ratings
findings.effect_size: 0.98 SD increase; 2.9-point gain; reliable improvement 21.6% in AI Coach vs 2.9% in control
findings.sample_size: n=968; Control N=245, AI Coach N=231, Combined N=247

findings.finding_summary: Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly improved LLM-evaluated encouraging elaboration relative to control, β=0.648, p<0.001. Combined training produced a comparable gain, β=0.621, p<0.001, while video instruction had a smaller effect, β=0.218, p<0.05; AI coach and combined training significantly outperformed video instruction on this prescriptive behavior.

Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly improved LLM-evaluated validating emotions relative to control, β=0.475, p<0.001. Combined training also improved validating emotions, β=0.613, p<0.001, and video instruction had a smaller significant effect, β=0.239, p<0.001.

Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly improved LLM-evaluated demonstrating understanding relative to control, β=0.459, p<0.001. Combined training improved this outcome, β=0.573, p<0.001, and video instruction also improved it with a smaller effect, β=0.247, p<0.001.

Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly reduced LLM-evaluated unsolicited advice giving relative to control, β=-0.679, p<0.001. Combined training produced a larger reduction, β=-1.038, p<0.001, while video instruction increased advice giving, β=0.205, p<0.05; pairwise comparison showed combined training reduced advice giving more than AI coach alone, difference=0.30 SD, z=3.27, p=0.002.

Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly reduced LLM-evaluated dismissing emotions relative to control, β=-0.451, p<0.001. Combined training also reduced dismissing emotions, β=-0.656, p<0.001, as did video instruction, β=-0.325, p<0.001.

Personalized feedback from the AI coach significantly reduced LLM-evaluated self-oriented responses relative to control, β=-0.213, p<0.05. The text reports significant AI coach reduction for this proscriptive behavior, while the combined-training reduction is not reported as significant for self-oriented responses.

In a second preregistered experiment, 150 Prolific participants made two-alternative forced-choice judgments over 150 conversations sampled from the Lend an Ear dataset. Human raters increasingly preferred conversations with higher LLM empathy scores as the score gap widened; logistic regression showed OR=1.155, 95% CI [1.12, 1.19], and Bradley-Terry human-preference rankings correlated with LLM scores, Spearman ρ=0.75, and LLM Elo ratings, Spearman ρ=0.85, both p<0.001.
findings.measure: Human preference agreement with LLM empathy scores and LLM Elo rankings
findings.effect_size: OR=1.155; Spearman ρ=0.75 with LLM empathy scores; Spearman ρ=0.85 with Elo ratings; p<0.001

quality_tier_rationale: The paper reports a preregistered randomized experiment with random assignment to control, video, AI coach, and combined conditions, plus a second preregistered human-rating validation experiment. Credibility concerns include reliance on automated LLM scoring for primary outcomes, a short-term/proximal outcome, an adult Prolific sample rather than K-12 learners, and preprint status.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported intervention effects were medium-to-large, including a 0.98 SD gain in overall empathic communication performance for the AI coach condition and standardized effects above 0.20 on all six preregistered communication dimensions. Effects were beneficial for both increasing prescriptive empathic behaviors and reducing proscriptive behaviors.
